input.quote: MSL agrees to protect, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify IBM from and against any and all claims, damages, liabilities, losses and expenses, arising out of the following, whether alleged or actual:
input.rationale: Section 15.1 gives us a vendor-side indemnity from MSL covering (a) third-party IP infringement (patent, trademark, trade name, copyright, mask work, trade secret) arising from MSL's performance, procured Parts, processes, designs, deliverables or pre-existing materials, (b) MSL's failure to comply with law, and (c) failure to perform its warranty/support obligations — the core of the preferred position. Exclusions are the usual ones (IBM-selected marks, IBM written specifications, IBM-provided defective designs), and Section 15.2 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation, MSL control with our right to participate at our expense) plus procure/redesign remedies at MSL's expense. There is no reciprocal IBM indemnity of MSL anywhere in the Agreement, and Appendix A §5 adds a further MSL indemnity for Microsoft code, so the allocation runs in our favour. Minor points noted but not flagged: the indemnity names IBM rather than IBM and its affiliates, and does not separately call out data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; also, the mutual 3%-of-bill-of-materials cap in Section 15.3(b) would on its face apply to indemnity recoveries — that cap is properly addressed under the limitation-of-liability rule rather than double-flagged here.
